title: Calendar heading: 1974
summary: The catalogue supplies a calendar-year divider, not a dated talk. Its overlapping page range contains the end of Kazhdan's previous entry, Springer's short entry, and the opening of Novikov's talk. No additional mathematical assertion is assigned to this heading. The academic-year prefix remains 1973.

speaker: T. A. Springer
title: Green polynomials
summary: Only the title and the distinction between a finite general linear group and its algebraic group over the algebraic closure survive. Neither a Green-polynomial formula nor a theorem of Springer can be recovered from this page.

speaker: S. P. Novikov
title: Periodic KdV, Floquet theory, and finite-gap potentials
summary: Novikov's continued talk interleaves Gelfand's explanation of Floquet decomposition with stationary KdV and its spectral curve. Distinct questions concern monotonicity inside bands, missing inverse-spectral data, and density of finite-gap potentials. Novikov's 1974 paper was received on 18 February, one week before this recorded session; its later journal appearance is distinguished from this prior manuscript date.

speaker: V. E. Zakharov
title: Dressing, compatible operators, and integrable wave equations
summary: The talk explains the Zakharov--Shabat dressing scheme through a Gelfand--Levitan equation, then obtains scalar and matrix nonlinear equations from compatibility. It includes KP, three-wave interaction, sine-Gordon, and nonlinear Schrödinger examples, and an unquantified Hamiltonian conjecture. The manuscript writes 1973 in the heading; catalogue chronology and adjacent dates require 1974. The general joint paper was received ten days after the talk, whereas Shabat's 1973 scalar precursor already existed.

speaker: A. Ya. Povzner
title: Whitham modulation of nonlinear waves
summary: Povzner presents Whitham's slowly modulated traveling-wave method for nonlinear Klein--Gordon equations. The one-page outline mixes fast and slow variables and gives an incompletely specified action relation. The identifiable reference is Whitham's 1970 article, although the notebook writes 1972.

speaker: V. N. Tulovskii
title: Hörmander wavefront sets and oscillatory integrals
summary: Tulovskii explicitly presents Hörmander's work: conic Fourier decay, kernel relations, distribution products, symbol estimates, and cutoff oscillatory integrals. The content matches the 1971 Acta paper, whose precursors include 1969 lectures. Gelfand contributes geometric explanations. The notebook's word 'continuous' must be read in the original sequential sense; its sign convention for kernel relations also needs repair.

speaker: A. B. Shabat
title: Soliton collisions, rational interpolation, and the Miura transformation
summary: Shabat discusses one- and two-soliton waves, collision amplitude and shifts, and an interpolation construction of polynomial-exponential Schrödinger solutions. Several signs, a nonlinear coefficient, and the interpolation normalization are inconsistent in the notebook; an auxiliary operator is literally left empty. Shabat's 2014 paper explicitly recalls this 1974 Gelfand seminar, making it an unusually strong provenance match, while its precise theorem also exposes the missing assumptions.

speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: Infinite-dimensional groups and symmetric Fock space
summary: This source-recovered supplementary entry has its own Kirillov heading on P000551. The official MCCME archive identifies record 331 but incorrectly dates it 25 March 1975; the folio clearly reads 25/III-74 between 18 March and 1 April 1974. Kirillov names diffeomorphism/current groups and bundle automorphisms, then sketches symmetric Fock space. No particular representation theorem survives.

speaker: B. M. Gurevich
title: KdV by Whitham modulation
summary: A second, separate heading on the same 25 March 1974 folio reads Gurevich, on the KdV equation by Whitham's method. The official archive identifies record 332 and B. M. Gurevich but shares record 331's erroneous 1975 date. No mathematical development follows the title. The famous A. V. Gurevich--Pitaevskii paper is a different author identity and supplies only thematic context.

speaker: Yu. Koblenz
title: Heat invariants, closed trajectories, and asymptotic spectral multiplicity
summary: Koblenz reports heat-trace coefficients through the fourth term and their curvature interpretation. Gelfand inserts an unresolved lattice-point analogy; Shnirelman introduces closed billiard paths. The discussion passes from heat to wave traces and to near-degenerate eigenvalue pairs. The all-indices two-torus statement has an exact primary match in Shnirelman's 1975 note, received 7 May 1974. Its square-root spectral parameter must be distinguished from the Laplacian eigenvalues at the start of the talk.
